title: Extension of a generic-fibre line bundle over a smooth DVR scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a smooth morphism of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $Y_K=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change]. Every invertible $\mathcal O_{Y_K}$-module extends to an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]: for each $L$ on $Y_K$ there exist $\widetilde L$ on $Y$ and an isomorphism $\widetilde L|_{Y_K}\cong L$. No uniqueness, properness, excellence or hypothesis on residue characteristic is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BD9 (lemma-extend-invertible-module); smooth schemes over a regular base are regular, descent.tex Tag 036D (lemma-regular-local-smooth); regular local rings are UFDs, more-algebra.tex Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD).

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$. The DVR definition makes $R$ Noetherian (each ideal is principal). Its dimension is one by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], so its principal maximal ideal makes $R$ regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Every nonzero prime ideal of the local PID $R$ is maximal, hence is its maximal ideal; localization at it is $R$, while localization at $(0)$ is $K$, a regular local ring of dimension zero. Thus $R$ is a regular ring.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), (1) implies (3); PID definition and regular-ring definition.

proof.text: By the affine-local description of smoothness in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] (Stacks 01V5), every point of $Y$ has an affine open neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ mapping into an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is smooth; by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] the ring map $B\to A$ is smooth. By Step 1, $\operatorname{Spec}R$ has exactly two points, $(0)$ and $\pi R$, so $V$ is either $\operatorname{Spec}R$ or the open point $\{(0)\}=D(\pi)$, whose ring is $R[1/\pi]=K$ (the identification of Step 4, which does not use this step). Both $B=R$ and $B=K$ are regular rings by Step 1 ($K$ is a field, regular local of dimension zero). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] to $B\to A$ proves that $A$ is regular and Noetherian. These opens show that $Y$ is regular and locally Noetherian [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Since the morphism is of finite type, $Y$ is quasi-compact ([def-weil-finite-type-morphism], preimage of the affine $\operatorname{Spec}R$), so finitely many such charts $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ cover $Y$.

source.place: Tag 036D (lemma-regular-local-smooth), ascent direction; affine proof via Algebra Tag 07NF.

proof.text: For every $y\in Y$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with the prime localization of the regular coordinate ring of a chart from Step 2. It is regular local by the definition of a regular ring. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] with the empty parameter list ($r=0$); its first conclusion says that this local ring is a UFD. The extra boundary and localization conclusions are unused.

Every nonzero $s\in R$ equals $u\pi^m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], so $a/s=(au^{-1})/\pi^m$ for every fraction in $K$. Thus $K=R[1/\pi]$: the map is injective since $R$ is a domain, and the displayed fractions prove surjectivity. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and its pullback $Y_K\to Y$ are open immersions. Identify $Y_K$ with this open $U$, and regard the given $L$ as an invertible module on $U$.

source.place: Tags 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion); Algebra Tag 00PD for the fraction calculation.

proof.text: Induct on $i$ to extend $L$ to $U_i=U\cup W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_i$, starting with $M_0=L$. Given $M_i$, put $W=W_{i+1}$ and $V=U_i\cap W$. The affine $W$ is Noetherian by Step 2; [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes its open $V$ Noetherian. It is quasi-affine because it is open in the affine $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-quasiaffine-line-effective-divisor] to obtain an effective Cartier divisor $D\subset V$ and an isomorphism $M_i|_V\cong\mathcal O_V(D)$. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 0BD9 (lemma-extend-invertible-module), affine-neighbourhood step; Tag 0AYM (lemma-quasi-projective-Noetherian-pic-effective-Cartier), quasi-affine case.

proof.text: Every local ring of $W$ outside $V$ is a UFD by Step 3 (restriction to an open preserves stalks). Apply [lem-sfb-cartier-extension-factorial-complement] to obtain an effective Cartier divisor $E\subset W$ restricting to $D$. Put $N=\mathcal O_W(E)$. Its restriction to $V$ is $\mathcal O_V(D)$: locally an effective Cartier ideal is generated freely by a nonzerodivisor $f$, its dual is generated by $f^{-1}$, and restricting this generator and its transition units gives the dual of the restricted ideal. Therefore Step 5 gives an isomorphism $M_i|_V\cong N|_V$.

source.place: Tag 0BD8 (lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor); definition of the associated invertible module.

proof.text: Glue $M_i$ on $U_i$ and $N$ on $W$ along that isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing], applied to the Zariski open site of $U_i\cup W$. Use the isomorphism on one ordered overlap, its inverse on the reverse overlap, and identities on equal-index overlaps; the cocycle follows by cancellation. The glued module $M_{i+1}$ is locally free of rank one because its restrictions to both opens are, hence is invertible. Retain its isomorphism with $M_i$ on $U_i$, so its restriction to $U$ is still $L$. After $n$ steps $U_n=Y$; set $\widetilde L=M_n$. For $Y=\varnothing$ take its structure sheaf. This yields the required extension and restriction isomorphism.
